basis: Deficiency of pituitary hormone production defines an endocrine disorder.
MELAS is a mitochondrial metabolic disorder defined by encephalopathy, stroke-like episodes, lactic acidosis and skeletal myopathy.
Persistent kidney damage and impaired renal function define CKD; associated anaemia and mineral-bone disorders are separately diagnosed complications.
Congenital skeletal myopathy with characteristic muscle inclusions; associated neurologic abnormalities lack evidence of frequency above 30%.
Developmental disability, heart defects and hearing loss define the syndrome; contractures and brachydactyly occur in 80-99%. Ocular dysfunction also qualifies (~67%), omitted by cap.
Immune destruction of transplanted tissue; the affected organ varies with the graft and cannot be assigned across this umbrella.
Vitamin D resistance causes defective skeletal mineralization and rickets; alopecia is occasional (5-29%).
Bradykinin-mediated subcutaneous and oral angioedema; lip and tongue edema occur in 30-79%. Airway obstruction and laryngeal edema are <30%; mechanism is nonimmune.
Cystic dilation of hepatic or extrahepatic bile ducts; both belong to the hepatic axis.
Physical stimuli induce mast-cell-mediated urticaria of the skin; no additional organ damage defines the umbrella.
Hypergonadotropic ovarian hormone failure and recurrent metabolic acidosis both fall within the endocrine-metabolic axis; short stature alone adds no skeletal axis.
Immunodeficiency and characteristic livedo/telangiectases define FILS. Recurrent respiratory infections do not establish chronic lung damage; bronchiectasis occurs in 2/14.
Sclerosis of skin; no evidence establishes an autoimmune mechanism or systemic organ involvement.
Lysosomal storage with neurodevelopmental decline; hearing impairment 5/11 (~45%). Dysphagia 4/11 may be neurogenic; documented skeletal abnormalities are <30%.
Resistance concerns inadequate aspirin inhibition of platelet function. Cardiovascular events are risks rather than defining direct organ damage.
Sarcoma originates in the penis, a reproductive organ outside the axes; individual vascular or muscular subtypes do not define the umbrella.
Psychiatric impulse-control disorder; the umbrella does not establish structural neurologic or other organ damage.
Fusion of carpal, tarsal and phalangeal bones defines the syndrome; hearing abnormality occurs in only 1/20 patients.
Benign epithelial tumour of the ovarian surface; reproductive origin without endocrine dysfunction.
Inborn mitochondrial respiratory-chain complex III deficiency; supplied evidence does not establish a common organ-specific injury pattern.
Mesothelial tumour arising in the abdominal peritoneal lining, assigned to the gastrointestinal axis; no other organ involvement established.
Primary cutaneous amyloid deposition causes progressive pigmentary skin lesions; systemic amyloidosis is explicitly absent.
Progressive cerebral neurodegeneration with dementia and cortical atrophy; occasional visual findings do not establish common ocular damage.
Developmental disability and hypergonadotropic hypogonadism define the syndrome; short stature and delayed skeletal maturation do not establish skeletal injury.
Immune-mediated juvenile polyarthritis; ANA negativity does not remove the immune mechanism. Uveitis is not common enough to add ocular involvement.
